doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: Working with different bassists and drummers and how he writes charts
summary: He wants cooperation and dynamics from rhythm sections and sends simple Finale charts with minimal instructions.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Because you get to play either by choice or by necessity with different bassists and drummers —
What would a bassist or a drummer do that might annoy you?

I find problems when they have too little personal input. If they always ask me what I want — sometimes in Asia they are fantastic. They do exactly what you say and that’s amazing of course, but I want it to be cooperation. So as I said, I play a lot with different rhythm sections. And I mean next week I’m going to play with a rhythm section in Vietnam and the week after that I’m going to Malaysia to play with a new rhythm section. My way of doing it is I try not to tell people too much what to do. I tell them to let us take the music where it goes. So I can be happy with a soft drummer, I can be happy with a loud drummer. As long as it’s not one dynamic all the time. So it’s not soft all the time or loud all the time or medium all the time. I do prefer dynamics in musicians. And when I get that I’m happy. And if you, you do your best to add some dynamics.
Well I’m guessing you give them more information than Thad Jones gave to you.

I definitely need to do that. I try to put, like Pepper Adams, very easy to read scores. I do Finale by computer. And I send PDFs. I could do a red circle, “last time to coda” circle. Here’s the coda. Okay? Play always this key or something like that. I say this style, this is even eighths, this is swing, this is a ballad. So I give some information in the scores, but not too much. The important — I mean of course it’s nice to get the forms right, that the bridge comes where the bridge should come. I mean that’s the basic. But apart from that, it can be very different from night to night and it can be different from rhythm section to rhythm section. Some songs I change. Some songs I can change tempo and character from day to day. Some songs I play more the same all the time.
Was the drummer reading the same chart as the bass player yesterday?
Yes. And I try not to send too complicated — I mean it’s another thing if I work with my own trio, I can work on totally other things. On meter, other kinds of arrangements. I
don’t want to make it too complicated. I want to be able to come into the music and communicate.
There’s nothing like watching the drummer and he’s got his music stand over here, and that’s where his focus is, on the music stand.
Yes, yes, yes. But that was the first time we’d played. But somewhat —he looked at me.
